channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: The Unexpected Portrait · Workshop13
item.description: Juried exhibition at ArtWorks Gallery, run by Workshop13, a nonprofit cultural arts and learning centre in Ware, Massachusetts. Artists are asked to deviate from formal posing and realistic representation, focusing instead on emotion, identity, memory, action or unconventional subject matter through modern techniques, stylised depiction or abstract interpretation of the sitter. Open to most physical media, photography included — electronic media cannot be accommodated, and AI-generated work, work created under instruction and work previously juried into an ArtWorks Gallery show are ineligible. Up to three original pieces per artist; the gallery may cap acceptances at two per artist depending on space. Juried by printmaker and teaching artist Julie Lapping Rivera. Accepted 2-D work must be framed and wired, hand-delivered or shipped with a prepaid return label. Exhibition runs 19 September – 17 October 2026, with an opening reception on 19 September. The gallery takes 30% commission on sales. — Deadline: August 20, 2026. Fee: $25 (1 work) / $35 (up to 3). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: West Coast Biennial 2027 · Turtle Bay Exploration Park
item.description: Ninth edition of Turtle Bay Exploration Park's juried West Coast Biennial, held in the museum galleries in Redding, California. Juror Karlo Henry Velazquez Fernandez — artist, curator, founder of The Art Hunger and Arts Director for Viva Downtown Redding — will select between 30 and 50 works for the exhibition. Painting, printmaking, drawing, photography, sculpture and mixed media are all accepted. Open to artists living in California, Oregon, Washington and Alaska, who may enter up to three works made within three years of the deadline. Cash awards are presented at the opening: Best of Show $3,000, First Prize $1,750, Second $900, Third $650, plus Honorable Mention and People's Choice awards of $325 each. The exhibition runs 29 January – 18 April 2027, opening with an artists' reception and juror talk. — Deadline: November 6, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: $3,000 + exhibition.

item.title: Artist Grant — November 2026 Cycle
item.description: An unrestricted $1,200 USD grant awarded to one visual artist three times a year, running since 2017. There is no proposal to write: applicants email a link to their website or three to five images of recent work along with a CV, resume or short bio. Open to visual artists aged 18 and over anywhere in the world working in painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, printmaking, photography, mixed media, installation and new or alternative visual art forms; film, video, music, theatre and dance are excluded, and past winners may not reapply. Grantees are featured on the Artist Grant website and social channels. Results are sent within six to eight weeks of the deadline. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: $1,200.

item.title: Reverie Magazine — Issue VI
item.description: Open submissions for the sixth issue of Reverie, an international independent literary and arts magazine whose stated mission is to promote education and amplify the voices of marginalised communities through literature and fine arts. Alongside poetry, prose and short fiction, the magazine reads visual art in all forms — contemporary photography, digital illustration, scans of painting and documentation of physical craft. Artists may send up to five high-resolution pieces as PNG, PDF or JPG to the editors by email, with a 50-word bio in the body of the message. Submissions are free and open worldwide. Previously published work is accepted if the prior publication is credited, and simultaneous submissions are welcome. Reverie asks for first publishing and archival rights; all rights revert to the maker on publication. Editors respond in about a month. — Deadline: August 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Cite the Past, Sight the Stars — Wigwell Lodge Residency · The Photographers' Gallery
item.description: Two-month fully funded residency at Wigwell Lodge in Derbyshire, run by The Photographers' Gallery in partnership with The Ampersand Foundation, for artists working with expanded photography and digital practices. Framed by photography's 200th anniversary, the call takes a set of speculative starting points — the Mnemosyne Atlas, the Voyager Golden Record, StarDisk, Inverted World Labs — and invites proposals that test ideas rather than deliver finished work. Suggested threads include image-making and celestial fictions, institutional archives, photography's relationship to computational culture, deep time, cosmic and earthly debris, transmissions and satellite imagery, and digital twins and AI world models. The residency provides accommodation and studio space at Wigwell Lodge, a £1,000 monthly stipend, a £1,000 production budget, up to £500 towards travel, promotion, and curatorial and administrative support, with the potential to develop into a commission for 2027/2028 and a public presentation at the Gallery or a partner venue. Open to individual artists over 18 with the legal right to work in the UK; no visa sponsorship is available. The residency runs 2 February – 31 March 2027. — Deadline: September 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £2,000 stipend + £1,000 production budget.

item.title: Brooklyn Darkroom Artist in Residence 2027
item.description: Travelling residency for analog photographers run by Brooklyn Darkroom, a New York State 501(c)(3) that supports film-based practitioners with photography and travel resources. Selected artists get up to one month on the road in 'Infared', a fully equipped 2023 Winnebago Solis 59P pop-top camper van, a $4,000 stipend covering travel, living and materials while travelling, and access to the organisation's analog darkroom in Brooklyn for development, printing and finishing, plus optional post-production support. Applications are open to all artists working in analog photography, and experimental collaborations are welcome; past residents include Curran Hatleberg, Irina Rozovsky, Mark Steinmetz, Jocelyn Lee and Dylan Hausthor. Applying costs $15 through SlideRoom. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: $4,000 stipend + One-month camper van residency.

item.title: Liberty Art Award 2026 · Liberty Specialty Markets
item.description: Two-year professional development, exhibition and sales programme for recent UK art graduates, run by fine art insurer Liberty Specialty Markets with Parker Harris. Launched in 2018 and previously limited to four institutions, the award opens to graduates nationwide for the first time this year. Each selected artist receives a £1,000 participation fee, a contribution to travel expenses, collection and return of work, insurance in transit and on display, and the chance to exhibit and sell work at Liberty's office in the Walkie Talkie building in Fenchurch Street, London, from September 2026 to August 2028. The development programme includes at least four one-to-one mentoring sessions with Penny Harris of Parker Harris, group visits to Frieze, London Art Fair, Collect and London Print Fair, seminars from gallerists, funders, curators, critics and legal advisors, and task-based work on proposal writing and funding applications. The programme closes with an awards ceremony in spring 2028. Any medium is eligible, including photography, moving image, print, sculpture, paint and textile; work must be available for the full two years and shown in a corporate setting. Open to students who graduated in 2025 and 2026 from across the UK. — Deadline: July 29, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £7,500 in prizes + £1,000 participation fee.

item.title: The People's Garden · Open Eye Gallery
item.description: Rolling open call from Open Eye Gallery in Liverpool, gathering the public's own garden pictures for The People's Garden, a growing display within the gallery's exhibition Is This A Garden? (26 June – 31 August 2026). The gallery welcomes family album photographs as readily as recent pictures — a family gathering, a football game, a visiting puppy, your own garden or a public one. Selected images are printed and added to the exhibition as they arrive, so earlier submissions hang for longer. Send up to three digital images at the highest resolution possible, 30MB maximum each, by email with your name, postcode, an optional text of up to 100 words about the images, and a statement confirming the images are your own and you have the right to show them publicly. No AI-generated or digitally manipulated images. Open to anyone over 18 currently based in the UK; one submission per person. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: In The Practice of Seeing — High School Section · Jacksonville State University
item.description: Free national juried photography exhibition for high school students, running as the teen section of Jacksonville State University's In the Practice of Seeing and shown in the Roundhouse Gallery at Hammond Hall alongside the main exhibition, 27 August – 24 September 2026. The brief treats photography as an active process of perception rather than a neutral record — seeing shaped by attention, context, memory and cultural framework. Open to all photographic processes including digital, film, alternative processes, mixed media incorporating photography, and photographic installations; every entry must originate from a camera-based capture or a cameraless photographic method such as photograms, cyanotypes or wet plate. Open to students aged 13–17. Up to 3 images, free to enter; framed work no larger than 16 × 20 inches, with artists responsible for shipping or delivery. Winners receive an Adorama Photo sponsored gift card. — Deadline: August 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Adorama gift card + Exhibition.

item.title: Eyes & Hands: Celebrating Frederick's Deaf heART · Artspiration Frederick
item.description: Juried exhibition for Deaf, Hard of Hearing and CODA (Children of Deaf Adults) artists at Artspiration Frederick, a nonprofit community art centre in Frederick, Maryland, marking Deaf Awareness Month. Artists are invited to submit original work in any visual medium including photography, painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, fiber art, ceramics, mixed media and digital art, with the show seeking a deliberately wide range of voices, perspectives, techniques and subject matter. On view in the Artspiration Frederick Gallery 5–27 September 2026. Open to visual artists 16 and older who are Deaf, Hard of Hearing and/or CODA and reside in the continental US; 1–3 images at 300 dpi for jury review. Two-dimensional work must be framed and wired for hanging — no sawtooth hangers. — Deadline: August 15, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Americana · Crooked Tree Arts Center
item.description: Juried exhibition in the East and West Carnegie Galleries at Crooked Tree Arts Center in Traverse City, Michigan, asking what America looks like through your eyes. Beyond the familiar shorthand of rolling farmland, front porches, Main Streets, county fairs and open roads, the call invites work that celebrates, questions, reinterprets or expands American identity — drawing on place, community, music, labour, history, culture, memory, migration, celebration, resilience and everyday life. Works may be literal or abstract, traditional or experimental; all media are welcome, photography included, and artists at every career stage are encouraged. Open to artists 18+ resident in the US Great Lakes region — if your state has a Great Lakes shoreline, you are eligible. Up to three works made in the last three years, $30 entry. Exhibition 4 September – 3 October 2026. — Deadline: July 30, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Leela Mukherjee Artist-Educator Grant 2026 · Mrinalini Mukherjee Foundation
item.description: Third edition of the Mrinalini Mukherjee Foundation's annual grant for artist-educators in India, instituted in 2024 with the support of the Welham Old Boys' Society and named for the modernist sculptor and teacher Leela Mukherjee, who introduced art to generations of students at Welham Boys' School in Dehradun. Three grants of Rs. 1 lakh each support practitioners running an art education project with school-aged children (5–18), inside or outside the classroom, over a period of up to 12 months. The foundation looks for projects that fold local knowledge, lived environments and everyday experience into teaching methods, and for artists whose own practice and pedagogy inform one another. Proposals should describe the student group and why the artist works with them, the innovative strategies and artistic methods proposed, expected outcomes after 12 months, a tentative budget and a timeline. Applicants must be Indian citizens resident in India and over 18; collectives may apply if every member qualifies. The foundation's grants are restricted to the visual arts, which include lens-based practice. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,200 (Rs. 1 lakh) × 3 grants.

item.title: III Artist Fund Grant 2026
item.description: Artist-run fund set up by Jamie Zimchek and Shannon Cleere, who met in graduate school and created the grant to support artists navigating a post-graduate practice at a moment when work that challenges dominant narratives faces scrutiny, funding difficulties, and censorship. A $1,000 unrestricted grant goes to one artist who holds an MFA in Visual Art awarded May 2025 or later and can demonstrate a strong research-based practice responding to contemporary contexts. Multidisciplinary and conceptual artists working in photography, drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, textile, installation, performance, sound, video and new media are all encouraged to apply. The recipient is asked only to give a short artist talk within six months, recorded and posted to the fund's website. — Deadline: August 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,000.

item.title: LSI 2026 Photography Grant · Leica Society International
item.description: Tenth edition of the Leica Society International's annual project-based grant, supported by the LSI Philanthropy Fund and Leica North America. The 2026 theme is 'To Be Seen': photographers worldwide are invited to submit an in-progress personal project in still images that creates space for people, places, communities, histories, or issues to be witnessed with care, dignity, and intention. Applications include a project description, a portfolio of 10 JPEG images from the project, a bio, and a CV. Judging runs in two phases — each juror ranks ten candidates from the qualified pool, then the jury meets to agree on a single winner from the ten finalists. The recipient receives $7,500 USD, a Leica camera and lens, and a gallery showing in Paris. Using a Leica camera is not required and LSI membership is not required. Entries are capped at 200 applications; the call closes on 4 September or when the cap is reached, whichever comes first. — Deadline: September 4, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $7,500 + Leica camera and lens.

item.title: Thinking Photography & Writing Photography 2026 · German Photographic Society (DGPh)
item.description: Biennial prizes for writing about photography, awarded jointly for the fourth time by the German Photographic Society (DGPh) and the Deutsche Börse Photography Foundation. The €3,000 'Thinking Photography' research prize honours scholarly work in photo theory and history — master's theses, dissertations, and independent publications alike, published or unpublished, created from November 2024. The €1,000 'Writing Photography' prize for innovative publicism recognises journalistic and essayistic publications on photography, with particular interest in blogs, columns, reviews, net-based formats, and work that creatively combines text and photographic material. Texts in German or English. Apply with an English summary (c. 3,500 characters), full manuscript, CV, and publication list via the upload links on the announcement page. An international jury decides; the awards are presented at a public event in 2027. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €3,000 + €1,000.

item.title: FOTOGALERIE WIEN — 2027 Annual Program
item.description: Vienna's artist-run association for the promotion of art photography and new media, founded 1981 and based at WUK, invites artists working in photography and new media to apply for its 2027 annual exhibition program. Send a portfolio as a single PDF (max 10 MB) documenting previous work or several current works or series — ideally including exhibition or installation views and technical details — together with a CV and/or biography. The curatorial collective reviews all submissions when composing the year's program of exhibitions. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: No! Wahala Magazine Issue 5: Interconnectedness
item.description: One of Africa's first contemporary photography magazines — a non-profit founded in 2020 by Anne and KC Nwakalor, dedicated to African photographers telling African stories on African terms. Issue 5 invites African photographers, on the continent and across its diasporas, to explore 'Interconnectedness': Pan-Africanism and shared histories, community and collective life, our relationship to land and environment, mind, body, and place. Documentary, conceptual, and experimental approaches all welcome. Submit a series of 10–15 individually captioned images with a written narrative as a Story on Visura. Window runs 1 July – 31 August 2026 (11pm GMT). AI-generated images are not accepted. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: HamOnt One Shot 2026 · Ponders Studios
item.description: A community photography competition timed to Supercrawl, Hamilton's big September arts festival: every eligible submission is professionally printed by 905 Print and hung at CoLodge on James Street North for the festival week, 9–13 September 2026. Up to five photos per entrant — any subject, any style, any camera, phones included. Gallery visitors rank their favourites for the People's Choice award, fellow entrants vote the Photographer's Choice, and Best Film Photograph and Best Black & White are also awarded. Winners in each category receive four additional 8×10 prints, a group show at Rooney's, and local prize packages. Optional $15 photo-book add-on includes your submitted photos in the official show book. Open to Ontario residents aged 18+. AI-generated imagery and generative fill are not accepted. Winners announced at the closing ceremony on 13 September. — Deadline: August 19, 2026. Fee: $15 CAD per photo. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: BROAD Magazine — Dreams Issue
item.description: Independent visual-culture photography magazine publishing themed print issues alongside its website and social feeds. For the Dreams issue, BROAD is after visual interpretations of dreams in every sense — the subconscious, the surreal, the symbolic, the personal, the political, the spiritual — living in the body, the landscape, family histories, imagined futures, and the fragile space between reality and illusion. Poetic, documentary, conceptual, experimental, and deeply personal approaches all welcome. A one-time $30 CAD community membership (not a recurring subscription) unlocks the project page for unlimited submissions during the window; the magazine is community-supported with no government funding or sponsorships. Selected contributors are contacted within two weeks after the deadline. — Deadline: August 10, 2026. Fee: $30 CAD membership (unlimited submissions). Prize: Publication.

item.title: Bibin Photography Magazine #6 — The Other
item.description: Quarterly contemporary photography magazine from Afghanistan. For Issue 6, psychology researcher Fatemeh Azizi interprets the selected photographs through an interdisciplinary approach, examining the relationship between the human and the Other — anything through which one experiences oneself in an encounter, from society and nature to objects and absence — via psychological and phenomenological readings of the image. Submit one photograph per entry (JPEG or PNG, max 3 MB, no logos, watermarks, or frames); no recognizable portraits, borrowed artwork, or merged frames. Multiple submissions welcome. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Tomorrow Will Be Yesterday · German Photographic Society (DGPh)
item.description: A photo slam presented by the German Photographic Society (DGPh) — a non-profit founded in 1951 with around 1,200 members — at Fotografiska Berlin to mark the society's 75th anniversary. Photographers worldwide, aged 18 and over, submit an existing photographic series of 10–20 images on the theme 'Tomorrow Will Be Yesterday': work that reads the present as raw material for tomorrow's memory — transition, emergence, transformation. Submissions include a short project description (max 600 characters) and a brief artist bio; files as JPEG, sRGB, 3000 px on the long side. Selected works are shown as a sequenced slideshow on the large LED wall at Fotografiska Berlin on 19 September 2026, and in an online slideshow the following day. Non-competitive — there is no cash prize. €15 per project; DGPh members submit free of charge via voucher code. — Deadline: August 21, 2026. Fee: €15 (free for DGPh members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: SHOTS Magazine #173 — Plant Life
item.description: Winter 2026 issue (#173) of the black & white photography quarterly, in print since 1986. Theme is Plant Life — broad, unusual and creative interpretations encouraged, no need to be literal. Submit up to 8 grayscale images at 300ppi (color files converted to B&W upon receipt). Free for current/renewing subscribers; $25 for non-subscribers ($28 international outside Canada). All processes, formats, and experience levels welcome; work submitted to previous issues may be resubmitted if unpublished. All submitting artists receive a complimentary copy of the issue. Initial selection by editor Elizabeth Flinsch. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free for subscribers / $25. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Crowded Table · OVERLAP Art Space
item.description: Juried exhibition at OVERLAP Art Space, a contemporary gallery in Newport, Rhode Island, on food and community — the cultivation, preparation, display and consumption of food, and the habits and traditions of nourishment and gathering. A range of mediums and subject matter is welcome, from topical work to functional 'tools for gathering'; the atmosphere is celebratory yet thoughtful. Jurors are Lesley Baker (Ceramics Department Head, RISD), Bob Dilworth (2025 Joan Mitchell Fellow, Professor Emeritus at University of Rhode Island), and Harry Philbrick (Executive Director, Newport Art Museum). Submit 1–3 images of 1–3 artworks with a short statement (max 250 words) on how the work relates to the theme. Exhibition November 14 – December 19, 2026; the holiday-season show is a fundraiser supporting OVERLAP and the Rhode Island Community Food Bank. The title comes from The Highwomen's 2019 song. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Nancy Ingersoll Foster Artist Residency 2026 · Oliver Art Center
item.description: An endowment-funded two-week retreat (September 5–19, 2026) presented by the Elizabeth Lane Oliver Center for the Arts, the nonprofit community art center on the Lake Michigan shore in Frankfort, Benzie County. Named for painter Nancy Ingersoll Foster, a longtime teacher and exhibitor at the center, the residency is housed at the Parsons Center for Arts and Sciences in Lake Ann — Eastern Michigan University's 86-acre arts-and-nature campus — with exhibits and workshops at the Oliver Art Center near the Sleeping Bear Dunes coastline. Open to an artist working in any visual media; applications are a short online form, due July 27. — Deadline: July 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency.

item.title: LACDA 2026 International Juried Competition
item.description: The relaunched flagship competition of the Los Angeles Center for Digital Art, the downtown LA gallery founded in 2004 that has collaborated with curators from MoCA, LACMA and the Hammer Museum. Open internationally to digital art and photography — any style where digital processes were integral to creating the image. The winner receives a solo exhibition in LACDA's main gallery (September 3–26, 2026) with a reception, plus ten museum-quality prints up to 44x60 inches (a $2,500–3,000 production value); all entrants get consideration for future LACDA group shows. Entry is $25 for three images ('back to 2004 price'), multiple entries allowed. Juried by founder and director Rex Bruce. — Deadline: August 17, 2026. Fee: $25 for 3 images. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: Art for the View 2026 · Sunnyview Rehabilitation Hospital Foundation
item.description: The 25th-anniversary edition of Sunnyview's exhibition of art and fine crafts by artists with disabilities. The show debuts at the Art for the View benefit evening at the Fenimore Gallery at Proctors Theatre in Schenectady on November 16, 2026, remains on display into December, and all work is for sale, with proceeds supporting the rehabilitation hospital's mission and the participating artists. Open to artists with physical, cognitive, visual and hearing disabilities; only work made after the onset of disability and completed within the last seven years is eligible. All media are welcome (no reproduction prints). Up to two pieces per artist; the application is short and free. — Deadline: August 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $500 Best in Show + Exhibition.

item.title: The Unexpected · Ashton Gallery @ Art on 30th
item.description: A regional juried show at Ashton Gallery inside San Diego's Art on 30th complex, on view August 22 – September 25, 2026, juried by Connect SD gallery owner Robert Plume. Sought: artwork that embraces unpredictability, accidents, transformation and unexpected outcomes. Photography is explicitly welcomed alongside 2D and pedestal-scale 3D work; no digital art, reproductions or AI-generated artwork (limited-edition photographic prints excepted). Enter digitally or drop off in person — jurors prefer in-person, and accepted online entries must be delivered to the gallery by Monday, August 17. All works must be for sale; the gallery takes 50% commission. Opening reception August 22. — Deadline: August 14, 2026. Fee: $35 up to 2, $45 up to 4, $55 up to 6. Prize: None listed.

item.title: South Florida Cultural Consortium Fellowship 2026
item.description: The arts councils of Broward, Martin, Miami-Dade, Monroe and Palm Beach counties jointly award grants of $7,500 or $15,000 to visual and media artists who have lived and worked in the five-county South Florida region for at least a year — among the largest regional artist awards in the US. Established in 1988, the consortium has granted over $4 million to more than 300 artists, with recipients' work presented in exhibitions. Photography and media work are eligible (samples from the past three years); degree-seeking students are not. Attendance at one of the remaining online workshops (August 4 or August 22) is required to apply. Funded in part by the National Endowment for the Arts and the State of Florida. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $7,500–$15,000 grants.

item.title: Frames Within Frames · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: Juried exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis on the frame within the frame — doorways, windows, mirrors, picture frames and architectural elements as the conceptual foundation of the image, creating layers of meaning, reflection, boundary and isolation. All genres and interpretations welcome. Up to 74 photographs are selected for the physical gallery show (September 19 – October 10, 2026). Awards include Juror's Choice (free entry into three future calls), Directors' Choice (two future calls) and eight honorable mentions featured in the exhibition, printed catalog and online gallery. Images shown at Praxis within the past year are ineligible; Praxis members get 10 images for the price of 5. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: $35 (5 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + catalog.

item.title: The Silent Cut: Moments in Motion · Fort Works Art
item.description: Juried exhibition at Fort Works Art, a contemporary gallery in Fort Worth, on cinematic ideas within still images — moments just before or after an action, sequencing that alters meaning, repetition, looping and compressed time. Emphasis on photography while open to all mediums; staged or documentary, sequential or singular. Selected works hang in an 11-week exhibition (October 24, 2026 – January 9, 2027) timed with the Lone Star Film Festival, with an opening reception. Open internationally; shipped works must arrive by October 17. — Deadline: September 19, 2026. Fee: $45 (up to 3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Tasweer Residency 2026–2027: As the Image Unfolds
item.description: The second edition of the residency from Tasweer, Qatar's photo festival organised by Qatar Museums. Three emerging photographers and visual storytellers based in Qatar, aged 21+, are selected for a five-month residency (1 October 2026 – 1 March 2027) at Bayt Al Wakrah in historic Old Al Wakrah City. Built around the concept of 'athar' — an Arabic word for traces, imprints and legacies — residents develop a project across documentary, conceptual, or experimental image-making. Each receives studio space at Bayt Al Wakrah, mentorship and professional development, access to local networks, and a monthly stipend of 4,000 QAR. Completed projects are presented in the exhibition 'As the Image Unfolds — The Language of Athar' during the 2027 Tasweer Photo Festival, accompanied by an online zine documenting the process. Apply with a cover letter, artist bio and statement, CV, a 15–20 image portfolio (PDF), a residency statement of intent, and 1–2 recommendation letters. Free to apply. — Deadline: September 3, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 4,000 QAR/month stipend + exhibition.

item.title: The Soldier's Lens 2026 · Florida Museum of Photographic Arts
item.description: FMoPA's second annual curated exhibition honoring military life, open to active-duty service members, veterans, and immediate family members. Free to submit up to 3 photographs capturing lived experience in and around military service; a panel versed in art and military service selects the show. Selected works are exhibited at FMoPA in Tampa November 5, 2026 – January 10, 2027, timed with Veterans Day, and featured in the museum's online gallery. All ages welcome (under-18s with parental consent). — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Museum exhibition.

item.title: Hand Fetish Projects — Issue #01: How to Survive in Southeast Asia
item.description: Founding print issue from independent arthouse Hand Fetish Projects, collecting images made from within Southeast Asia — humidity, density, informal architecture, urban exhaustion — alongside outside encounters with the region. Illustration, photography and mixed-media work is welcome, with experimental and analogue approaches encouraged; submit up to 3 works with a short artist statement. Selected artists receive the print-ready PDF edition free, physical copies at production cost, full copyright retained, and credit in the HFP archive. Publication expected September 2026. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: Delfina Foundation — Mondriaan Fund Netherlands Residency 2027
item.description: Three-month residency at Delfina Foundation in London (September 27 – December 17, 2027) for visual artists and curators who are Dutch or based in the Netherlands, organised in partnership with the Mondriaan Fund. Artists receive €9,188 and curators €7,232 toward travel, materials and living costs, with studio and accommodation paid directly to Delfina; residents contribute 10% personally. Apply in English via the Mondriaan Fund's digital application system. Deadline August 27, 2026, before 16:00 Dutch time. — Deadline: August 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency.

item.title: In Community: LACP's Annual Members' Exhibition
item.description: The Los Angeles Center of Photography's annual members' exhibition, open to current LACP members — membership can be purchased online before submitting. Juror Chandra Glick, Photo Director at Artforum, selects works for the show at LACP's downtown Los Angeles gallery, October 1–November 5, 2026, with an opening reception on October 1. Prizes: 1st place $500 cash; 2nd place $250 LACP gift card plus a one-year membership; 3rd place $250 LACP gift card; honorable mentions also awarded. Entry fees are tiered from $18.75 for a single image to $150 for 31–35 images. Images and texts created by AI are not accepted. — Deadline: August 11, 2026. Fee: $18.75–$150. Prize: $500 cash + exhibition.

item.title: Dek Unu Magazine — November 2026 Issue
item.description: International not-for-profit journal publishing one accomplished artist per monthly issue in print and online paperback. All fine art projects in all photo genres and techniques are welcome — each feature pairs 11 images with per-image commentary and an in-depth interview. Technical excellence paired with artistic vision and conceptual intent. Submission window for the November issue runs September 1–20, 2026; email submissions. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Photo Trouvée Magazine Issue 21 — Garden of Nostalgia
item.description: Print Issue 21 open call themed 'Garden of Nostalgia' for artists who work with or are inspired by vintage found or family photographs — florals, plants, connections to nature, or reflections on roots. Any media accepted. Selected artists receive a designated page spread with artist statement, a complimentary digital issue, and website, newsletter and social media features. The $40 publishing fee (due late October if selected) funds printing, design and a scholarship fund. International submissions welcome. — Deadline: October 10, 2026. Fee: Free to submit; $40 if selected. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: SlowExposures 2026 — Book Fair
item.description: Showcase and sell your photography book during the SlowExposures festival weekend — Saturday, September 19, 1–3 PM at the historic R.F. Strickland Building in Concord, Georgia. Open to the first 10 photographers who register; in lieu of a fee each participant donates one book, featured in the festival's print raffle at the Saturday evening dinner. Participants present their work to a public audience, with promotion through the festival's channels. — Deadline: September 19, 2026. Fee: Free (donate one book). Prize: Festival exhibition.

item.title: Raghu Rai MA-g Awards for Photography 2026 · Museum of the Avant-garde
item.description: The Museum of Avant-garde's annual photography award, chaired in 2026 by the Raghu Rai Foundation in his honour following his passing. Open to all — professionals, students and enthusiasts — on any theme; winning and shortlisted works are selected for the Museum's contemporary collection and featured online and in future exhibitions. The MA-g Awards name each edition after its judges; past photography jurors include William Klein, Nobuyoshi Araki, Graciela Iturbide and Antanas Sutkus. Photography entry is €55 single / €110 series, with early-bird, student and low-income-country discounts. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: €55–110. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Monochrome · Aurea Photogallery
item.description: Aurea Photogallery's black-and-white open call, asking photographers to leave colour behind and work with light, shadow, shape and texture alone. Portraits, landscapes, quiet street work and abstract shadows are all welcome, with an emphasis on strong contrast and raw emotion. Selected work runs in a one-month online exhibition (18 August – 14 September 2026) with a PDF and print-on-demand catalogue, a dedicated artist page and permanent inclusion in the gallery's archive. Submissions are reviewed on a rolling basis. — Deadline: August 12, 2026. Fee: Free (€30 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + Catalog.

item.title: 2027 Small Stones Festival of the Arts
item.description: Eighth edition of the juried festival run jointly by the Worcester County Camera Club and the Blackstone Valley Art Association, held in a restored barn outside Worcester. Fine art photography is judged as its own category — film, digital, infrared and alternative processes all eligible — with its own jurors and prizes, alongside fine art painting. 144 works are selected for the in-person exhibition and printed in a hardbound catalogue; all entries appear in the online Web Gallery. Work must be hand-delivered, and framed pieces are capped at 26 inches on the longest edge. The art call opens 1 September 2026. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $10/entry. Prize: Exhibition + Cash awards + Catalog.

item.title: Open Call for Exhibitions — Prospekto and Vilnius Photography Galleries
item.description: The Lithuanian Photographers' Association invites artists and curators to propose solo, group or curatorial photography exhibitions for its two Vilnius spaces — Prospekto Gallery on Gedimino Avenue and the Vilnius Photography Gallery. Applications are accepted year-round with no fixed deadline; selections are made once a year, in August. Submit an exhibition proposal of up to 500 words naming the preferred gallery and exhibition period, a bio of up to 100 words, and a portfolio with supporting visual material such as documentation of previous installations. Total submission size must not exceed 5 MB. Free to enter. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: Spotlight Awards 2026
item.description: Production Paradise's annual commercial and advertising photography awards, now in their ninth edition. The real draw is the jury: more than fifty picture editors, art buyers, creative directors and brand leads from IKEA, The Economist, Volvo Cars, Unilever, Louis Vuitton, Cartier, Ogilvy, Droga5, UNICEF, The Guardian and Mattel. Entrants opt in to having their work shown to every judge, and the organisers pitch it as a hiring channel as much as a competition — winner or not. Fifteen categories, one of them for AI-developed imagery. Each submission is a single image, commissioned or personal work, open to photographers in all countries over 18. The Grand Prize winner takes $1,000 cash plus a portfolio review ticket and strategy sessions; category winners receive sponsor packages, with a total prize pool over $40,000. Shortlists are announced from 1 September, winners on 22 September 2026. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: €35 first entry, €25 each additional. Prize: $1,000 + Portfolio review.

item.title: Global Reporting Grants
item.description: The Pulitzer Center's open, catch-all reporting grant — no restriction on topic or region — funding in-depth journalism on systemic issues that get too little coverage. Photographers are explicitly eligible alongside reporters, audio and video journalists and documentary filmmakers; staff and freelancers of any nationality can apply. Grants cover reporting costs against a reasonable, detailed budget; most awards for international travel fall between $5,000 and $10,000. It does not fund staff salaries, equipment purchases, books, feature-length films, routine breaking news or data projects aimed solely at academic research. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with no deadline; half the grant is paid once paperwork is complete and the remainder on submission of the finished work. Grantees join the Center's reporting network and its education and outreach programs. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000–$10,000.

item.title: Solo Project Space #8 · Drawing Rooms
item.description: Drawing Rooms hands over its Project Space and up to four further gallery areas to artists with a cohesive body of work or an installation — any theme, any concept, any size or medium, photography included. One artist takes the main Project Space and up to four more are given solo areas in the Jersey City galleries for the autumn slot, September 10 – October 11, 2026, with an opening reception on September 12 and a closing reception on October 11. Selected artists may also be picked up for other Drawing Rooms programmes, including The Art Project and the gallery's Artsy.net exhibits. Work must be original and available for sale, with 60% of proceeds to the artist. — Deadline: August 11, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: 10th SIPF Photo Market 2026 — Call for Exhibitors
item.description: The Singapore International Photography Festival opens its Photo Market to publishers, artists, collectives and creatives who want to show and sell photobooks, self-published zines, journals, prints, art objects and photography merchandise. The market runs across the opening weekend of the 10th SIPF biennale, October 17–18, 2026, within walking distance of the festival's main exhibition venues and free for the public to enter. Booths include a table and two chairs for up to two people, with a reduced Young Creatives rate for current students and graduates of the past three years; a hardship option can be flagged in the form. The market is curated and applications are assessed on a rolling basis, with no payment due until an application is successful. — Deadline: August 7, 2026. Fee: SGD 120–200. Prize: Exhibition booth.

item.title: Anthology Cover Art Competition 2026
item.description: Anthology, an Irish print magazine covering art, interiors, travel and literature, runs this competition to find the image for a future cover. Photography is judged alongside painting, printmaking, mixed media and digital work by an independent panel, so the winning image has to hold a whole cover on its own terms. The winner receives €500, the cover itself, and editorial coverage in print and online. Single images only, with unlimited separate entries; work already used on another publication's cover is ineligible, as is anything made with generative AI. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: €18. Prize: €500 + Publication.

item.title: A Show of Heads 2026 · Limner Gallery
item.description: SlowArt Productions' long-running annual exhibition at Limner Gallery in Hudson, New York, devoted to every reading of the human head — traditional portraiture, abstraction, caricature, the conceptual and the surreal. Photography sits alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, graphics, digital work, video and installation, with wall pieces up to 72 by 120 inches. Four works are covered by the entry fee and further works cost $5 each. Accepted artists pay nothing further: the show runs October 8–31, 2026 in the gallery and online, with a 35% commission on sales at prices the artist sets. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Guest Room: Whitney Hubbs & Jermaine Francis · Der Greif
item.description: The latest edition of Der Greif's monthly curator-led open call, guest-curated by artists Whitney Hubbs and Jermaine Francis. The brief asks for work exploring the materiality of photography and its spatial possibilities — an invitation to treat the photograph as an object and a situation rather than a window. Up to five images per project may be submitted, along with video up to ten minutes. Selected work is featured in Der Greif's online showcase, and selected artists also receive an online portfolio review with the curators. Submission is through Picter and the fee is genuinely voluntary — enter for free or donate €5 or €10. — Deadline: August 17, 2026. Fee: Free (optional €5 or €10 donation). Prize: Publication.

item.title: Preserving the Spirit · artCentral
item.description: A juried photography exhibition marking the 100th anniversary of Route 66, presented by artCentral in Carthage, Missouri — itself a Route 66 town. The call invites photographers to capture the highway in all its forms: neon-lit motels, vintage gas stations, vast landscapes, small-town main streets and the people who embody the road's enduring character. Creative edits are allowed, but work must be photographic, Route 66 inspired, framed and wired for hanging, and available for sale. Open to photographers 18 and over nationwide; up to three works may be submitted for jury consideration. The exhibition runs September 25 – October 30, 2026. — Deadline: September 5, 2026. Fee: $35 + $5 each addl. Prize: Exhibition.
